source.title: Some open questions on morphological operators and representations in the deep learning era: A personal vision

accepted.question_text: For nonlinear image transforms defined on complete lattices, can Matheron-Maragos-Banon-Barrera (MMBB) neural-network architectures effectively learn a minimal basis of structuring functions whose dilations, erosions, anti-dilations, and anti-erosions approximate any nonlinear image transform, and how should hierarchical deep-learning architectures be adapted for such MMBB networks?
accepted.context_brief: MMBB networks and learned structuring-function bases

evidence.quote: How effective MMBB networks would be to learn the minimal basis of structuring functions approximating any nonlinear image transform? How the idea of hierarchical architectures from deep learning can be used in the case of MMBB networks?

accepted.question_text: Can MMBB networks, whose primitives are lattice-theoretic morphological operators, be combined with standard deep-learning layers such as convolution, downsampling, upsampling, max-pooling, and ReLU to form relevant learnable pipelines?
accepted.context_brief: Hybrid MMBB and standard deep-learning pipelines

evidence.quote: Can MMBB networks be combined with standard layers in deep learning pipelines, providing relevant learnable models?

accepted.question_text: What unified algebraic models can integrate standard deep-learning layers with morphological layers so that deep-learning architectures can be studied mathematically, including questions about order continuity, invariance, fixed points, decomposition, simplification, and the expressiveness of deep MMBB networks and hybrid deep networks?
accepted.context_brief: Unified algebraic theory for hybrid deep networks

evidence.quote: What kind of unified algebraic models, integrating standard layers and morphological layers can be used to mathematically study deep learning architectures? Is there any information on order continuity, on invariance and fixed points, on decomposition and simplification, etc., which can be inferred from these unified algebraic models? What is the expressiveness of deep MMBB networks and the hybrid deep networks?

accepted.question_text: What Lipschitz morphological layers can be introduced into deep neural networks to control their Lipschitz constants and regularity, and can these morphological regularizing layers replace standard nonlinearities such as pooling plus ReLU without degrading network expressiveness?

evidence.quote: What kind of Lipschitz morphological layers can be introduced into deep networks to control their Lipschitz constant and therefore their regularity? Can these morphological regularizing layers replace the standard nonlinearities like pooling+ReLU without degrading their expressiveness?

accepted.question_text: Do deep networks that integrate morphological layers require fewer training examples than standard deep-learning architectures when learning Gestalt-pattern-theory-inspired visual concepts such as shape or symmetry?
accepted.context_brief: Sample efficiency of morphological layers for Gestalt-like tasks

evidence.quote: Are networks integrating morphological layers more ‘intelligent’ (i.e., requires less training samples) than standard deep learning architectures to learn tasks inspired from Gestalt pattern theory?

accepted.question_text: How efficiently can the generalized Tailor problem, the problem of decomposing any shape according to a set of templates, be solved by networks inspired by morphological iterative algorithms and group morphology?
accepted.context_brief: Generalized Tailor problem with morphological networks

evidence.quote: A combinatorial shape problem called generalized Tailor problem [60], which is connected to the one of finding the decomposition of any shape according to a set of templates, can be relevant to assess the interest of group morphology in deep learning based part-based decomposition. How efficiently can the generalized tailor problem be solved using networks inspired from the morphological iterative algorithm?

accepted.question_text: Are compact morphological representations of sets, such as skeleton-based representations, extrema of signed distance functions, and shape-size distributions from granulometries, more efficient for handling permutation invariance in machine-learning tasks on sets or graphs, and can loss functions based on such morphological descriptions be made inherently permutation-invariant and scale-invariant?
accepted.context_brief: Morphological set representations and invariant losses

evidence.quote: Are morphological compact representations of sets more efficient to deal with permutation invariance in machine learning? Can we introduce loss functions based on morphological descriptions which are inherently permutation-invariant and scale-invariant?

accepted.question_text: Can persistence or extinction-value features associated with image topology be learned for topological image classification and segmentation by using morphological reconstruction operators, and what architecture should implement the needed iterative reconstruction process, such as a residual architecture, recurrent architecture, or another design?
accepted.context_brief: Learning topological extinction features with reconstruction

evidence.quote: Can we learn persistence (extinction values) features to be used in topological image classification and segmentation using morphological operators based on reconstruction? Which architecture to be used for the iterative-based reconstruction (residual, recurrent, other)?

accepted.question_text: For interpretable deep-learning template extraction, what formulation of the hit-or-miss transform gives learnable and robust template-extraction layers, how efficient is the integration of hit-or-miss layers into complex deep architectures, should such layers be limited to the first layers, how should pattern-detection equivariance be handled using group-morphology-based hit-or-miss transforms, and what other morphological template-extraction operators are relevant as interpretable deep-learning layers?
accepted.context_brief: Hit-or-miss and related interpretable template layers

evidence.quote: What is the best formulation for the hit-or-miss transform to provide easy learnable and robust template extraction layers? How efficient is the integration of hit-or-miss layers into a complex architecture of deep learning? Only as the first layers? How to deal with equivariance in pattern detection by means of group morphology-based hit-or-miss transforms? What other morphological template extraction operators [62] are relevant as interpretable layers in deep learning?

accepted.question_text: Can architectures based on parametric families of morphological multiscale operators be learned efficiently while giving better interpretability for shape-recognition or texture-recognition tasks, and which parametric structuring functions are most useful in deep learning, such as quadratic functions defined by a shape covariance matrix or convex functions defined by Minkowski addition of oriented segments?

evidence.quote: Are there architectures based on parametric families of morphological multiscale operators which can be efficiently learned and provide a better interpretation on tasks of shape or texture recognition? What parametric families of structuring functions are the most fruitful in deep learning: quadratic ones defined by a shape covariance matrix? Convex ones defined by Minkowski addition of oriented segments?

accepted.question_text: In generative adversarial networks for image generation or microstructure simulation, can Choquet capacity be used in discriminators to impose morphological constraints learned from empirical data, and can GAN generators incorporate deconvolution-like image simulation closer to morphological random-set models by using morphological layers?
accepted.context_brief: Choquet capacity and morphological random-set constraints in GANs

evidence.quote: Can the notion of Choquet capacity play a role in the GAN discriminators to explicitly impose morphological constraints learned from the empirical data? Can one incorporate a ‘deconvolution’ image simulation closer to the morphological random set models into the GAN generators, thanks to the use of morphological layers?

accepted.question_text: For ultrametric convolutional neural networks operating on dendrogram or rooted-tree representations of data, how can the convolution operation be learned efficiently, how should max-pooling and unpooling layers be defined, and are there additional layers specifically useful for this type of neural network?

evidence.quote: How to efficiently learn the convolution operation on ultrametric convolutional neural networks? How to define the max-pooling and unpooling-layers on ultrametric convolutional neural networks? Are there specific layers useful in this kind of neural networks?

accepted.question_text: For hybrid networks that include morphological layers, is there an efficient learning technique that combines optimization inspired by tropical geometry with stochastic gradient descent, what gradient-descent optimizers work best, and can alternating optimization between convolution layers and morphological layers improve training?

evidence.quote: Is there any efficient network learning technique which can combine the optimization techniques inspired from tropical geometry and stochastic gradient descent? What are the best gradient-descent optimizers in the case of hybrid networks including morphological layers? Is there any strategy of alternate optimization between the convolution layers and the morphological layers?

accepted.question_text: Which smooth approximation to max-min-based morphological operators, such as counter-harmonic means or Log-Sum-Exp terms, is most relevant for training hybrid deep-learning networks whose learned nonlinearities may behave either like standard convolutions or like morphological operators?
accepted.context_brief: Smooth approximations for trainable morphological operators

evidence.quote: Which smooth approximation to morphological operators is more relevant for training deep learning hybrid networks?

accepted.question_text: Can genuine discrete layers, motivated by discrete geometry and binary, ternary, or integer-only neural-network representations, be incorporated into neural networks and trained with gradient-descent approaches, or are discrete-optimization approaches better suited to such networks?

evidence.quote: Is it possible to incorporate genuine discrete layers and to train them using gradient-descent approaches? Are there other approaches from discrete optimization better adapted to these networks?

accepted.question_text: Which numerical schemes for morphological partial differential equations are relevant for learning morphological operators or other nonlinear layers in deep-learning pipelines, how should the iterative nature of the approximations be handled, and can numerical schemes for morphological PDEs of matrix fields be used to learn nonlinearities for symmetric positive definite matrices or other matrix-valued data in Riemannian deep learning?
accepted.context_brief: Morphological PDE schemes as neural-network layers

evidence.quote: What numerical schemes for morphological PDEs are relevant in order to learn morphological operators or another non-linear layer? How to deal with the iterative nature of the approximations? Can the numerical schemes for morphological PDEs of matrix fields be used to learn non-linearities for SPD, or other matrices, in Riemannian deep learning?

accepted.question_text: For morphological artificial intelligence based on a morphological language of operators and structuring elements, what coding is most appropriate for natural-language-processing techniques, should operators and structuring elements be represented as inflected forms or separate words, what decomposition granularity preserves semantic interpretability while remaining learnable, is there a large enough corpus of morphological programs to learn operator embeddings, how can programs be extracted and parsed from multiple repositories, how can syntactical transformations simplify and rewrite morphological programs, and how can combinatorial and deep-learning techniques be integrated to search large program spaces efficiently?
accepted.context_brief: NLP and program-synthesis approaches to morphological AI

evidence.quote: What is the most appropiate coding of the morphological language to be use with NLP techniques? Is it efficient to use a word for the operator and a declination for the structuring element? Or to use different words for operator and structuring element? What is the optimal granularity on the decomposition of the operators to obtain a language with a high enough semantic interpretation and which can be still learnt? Do we have a large enough corpus of morphological programs available to learn the operator2vect embeddings? How to extract and parse morphological programs available in multiple repositories to train the algorithms? How can one introduce syntactical transformations to simplify and rewrite a morphological program? How to integrate combinatorial and deep learning techniques to explore large enough program spaces which can provide an efficient morphological AI?
